section_summary: This section covers proposed Japanese freight services, a possible change to a Japanese passenger ship’s sailing schedule, and new Japanese laws governing marine transportation associations and shipbuilding finance. Later reports describe the consolidation of Japan–China coastal shipping and the launch of two merchant vessels at Nagasaki. It also contains brief file notes, an internal memorandum, and a fragment of a separate letter about an incident at a mission in China.

subfiles.title: Document file note on proposed round-the-world Japanese freight line
subfiles.about: Points to Heath’s despatch and a conversation with Inman H. Payne.
subfiles.summary: Cross-references a despatch on a proposed Japanese freight line.

subfiles.title: Proposed round-the-world Japanese freight line
subfiles.from: Donald R. Heath, American Embassy, Berlin
subfiles.about: Transmits a memorandum of Payne’s account of a contemplated Japanese freight service.
subfiles.summary: Heath forwards a memorandum of his conversation with Cosmopolitan Shipping vice president Inman H. Payne.

subfiles.title: Memorandum of conversation with Inman H. Payne
subfiles.about: Records Payne’s account of a proposed Japanese round-the-world freight service.
subfiles.summary: Payne describes a proposed biweekly route through Suez, Germany, New York and Panama, and says its Japanese backers seek an American connection.

subfiles.title: Possible change in Nippon Yusen Kaisha sailing schedule
subfiles.from: M. Kelly, U.S. Naval Attaché, The Hague
subfiles.about: Reports a possible cancellation of the Katori Maru’s June sailing.
subfiles.summary: A confidential source reports possible schedule changes; the attaché speculates that Katori Maru might be retained as a transport.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on Japanese shipping-law translations
subfiles.about: Commends the attached translations and citations of Japanese shipping law.
subfiles.summary: Calls the report a valuable contribution to the Maritime Commission.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of translations of laws relating to the shipping industry
subfiles.from: Eugene H. Dooman, American Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Transmits and explains two Japanese laws on shipping associations and shipbuilding finance.
subfiles.summary: Dooman explains that the association law replaces voluntary bodies with government-directed organs. The shipbuilding law broadens access to state-backed loans and compensates lenders for losses to support fleet expansion.

subfiles.title: Law Relating to Marine Transportation Associations
subfiles.about: Sets out Japanese rules for establishing, governing and supervising marine transportation associations.
subfiles.summary: Law No. 69 defines marine transportation businesses and provides for associations and federations, including government-directed formation and compulsory membership in specified circumstances. It regulates officers, meetings, finances, supervision, dissolution and registration. Later articles prescribe fines and penalties, including for bribery; an Imperial Ordinance will set the enforcement date.

subfiles.title: Shipbuilding Capital Accommodation and Compensation for Losses Law
subfiles.about: Authorizes Japanese government support and loss compensation for shipbuilding loans.
subfiles.summary: Law No. 71 authorizes funding agreements with financial institutions for ten years from 1939. It specifies loan repayment and security rules, provides government compensation for 70 percent of qualifying losses, and permits payment in national bonds.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference note on discrimination against American shipping
subfiles.about: Points to another file for information on Japanese discrimination against American shipping.
subfiles.summary: References the original paper filed at 800.8890/687.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on consolidated Japan–China coastal shipping
subfiles.about: Notes the new Japanese shipping firm and the possibility of excluding foreign carriers.
subfiles.summary: Summarizes Peiping despatch 2222 and notes limited American shipping interests on the affected routes.

subfiles.title: Japanese shipping along the China Coast
subfiles.from: Frank P. Lockhart, American Embassy, Peiping
subfiles.about: Reports formation of Toa Kaiun Kaisha and considers its effect on foreign shipping.
subfiles.summary: Nine Japanese firms contribute 59 vessels to a consolidated company serving routes between Japan and China and along the China coast. The despatch details its planned offices and services, cites government support, and raises concern that it may disadvantage foreign carriers. It observes that no Chinese interests appear to be included.

subfiles.title: Launching of N.Y.K. motorship Sakura Maru
subfiles.from: Walter P. McConaughy, American Consul, Nagasaki
subfiles.about: Reports the launch and expected completion of the cargo vessel Sakura Maru.
subfiles.summary: The 7,100-ton Sakura Maru was launched at Nagasaki on December 13 for Nippon Yusen Kaisha’s European service.

subfiles.title: Letter concerning Japanese troops at a Southern Baptist mission
subfiles.to: First Secretary, Embassy of Japan, Peiping
subfiles.about: Relays a consular report of Japanese soldiers entering mission property and taking small articles.
subfiles.summary: The surviving page describes soldiers entering mission buildings, alarming residents and taking belongings.

subfiles.title: Launching of steamship Kofuku Maru
subfiles.from: Walter P. McConaughy, American Consul, Nagasaki
subfiles.about: Reports the launch and specifications of the coastwise steamship Kofuku Maru.
subfiles.summary: The 1,925-ton Kofuku Maru was launched at Nagasaki on December 14 for Daiko Shosen.
